territorial_scope.description: Applies to children defined as natural persons under 18 who reside in California; the text does not state a location test for developers or deployers.

evidence.quote: “Child” means a natural person under 18 years of age who resides in this state.

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Establishes a LEAD for Kids Standards Board and imposes risk-based duties on developers and deployers of AI systems used by or applied to Californian children: registration, assessments, labels, incident reports, audits and limits on child data use, from 1 July 2028. Enforced through Attorney General civil penalties and child lawsuits.
summary.long: Adds Chapter 25.1 (the LEAD for Kids Act) to the Business and Professions Code. It creates the LEAD for Kids Standards Board, which must adopt regulations by January 1, 2028 on risk levels (prohibited, high, moderate, low), assessments, information labels, audit standards, incident reporting and a public registry. By July 1, 2028, developers of covered AI products must register them, submit risk assessments, issue labels and report incidents within 30 days. Covered products are subject to independent third-party audits from July 1, 2028. Prohibited-risk products require reasonable steps to keep children from accessing them. Developers may not knowingly or recklessly use a child's personal information for training without consent of the child (aged 13 to under 16) or parent or guardian (under 13). Developers, deployers and contractors may not retaliate against employees who report violations to the Attorney General. The Attorney General may seek $25,000 civil penalties per violation after board referral, and children harmed by a covered product, or their parents, may bring civil actions for damages. Registration fees may not exceed regulatory costs. Duplicative requirements under other state risk-assessment laws need not be met.

evidence.quote: “Biometric information” has the meaning defined in Section 1798.140 of the Civil Code.

notes: The section header '2757.23.' is printed without the leading '2'; it is annotated as 22757.23. The document is the introduced text and contains only SECTION 1 (a new chapter), with no operative-date clause. The 'developer' and 'deployer' definitions overlap, since each can cover the other role. Civil Code targets are not in the registry, so target_instrument_id is empty.
